The anonymous Power of Mesmerism, dated 1891 and printed for the Nihilists at Moscow, is a Victorian erotic novel centered on Brackley Hall in Devon. Mr. Etheridge, a handsome man of forty with Italian blood, owns the fine old house and its wooded park running down to the coast. His wife, descended from an old Spanish family and married at sixteen, now stands in her thirty-fifth year.

Their daughter Ethel, just home from school in Paris at seventeen, mirrors her mother, while son Frank returns from study in Germany. The tale uses mesmerism as its engine for seduction and intrigue within the household. Readers get a period curiosity, frank in its subject and melodramatic in its telling.

Physicist Brian Greene returns to the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 1631. Greene, author of The Elegant Universe, is the public face of string theory, the attempt to unite all of physics in one framework of tiny vibrating strings. His talks are the show's deepest dives into the cosmos.

He and Rogan work through strings, extra dimensions, and the multiverse, ideas Greene explains with a storyteller's gift. Rogan asks what such a universe means for a human life inside it. The episode rewards patient listeners: a long, lucid tour of reality's basement, led by the man who wrote its most loved guidebook.
podcast-joerogan-shmDI4tMeuo:
Anthropologist Michael P. Masters presents his time-traveler theory of UFOs in episode 2428 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Masters, a professor, argues in his book Identified Flying Objects that the visitors may be us. On his view, the classic alien is a far-future human.

Masters explains how evolution could shape future humans toward the big heads and small bodies witnesses describe. He ties reports of craft to time machines rather than starships. Rogan probes the biology and the physics, asking what proof could ever settle it. The talk offers one of the strangest serious theories in the UFO debate.

Explorer Timothy Alberino joins Joe Rogan for episode 2530 to talk giants, Nephilim, and hidden history. Alberino leads expeditions and makes films about ancient mysteries in remote places. His work links Bible stories of giants to bones and ruins reported around the world.

Alberino lays out the reports and sites he says point to a lost, larger race of humans. He connects the Nephilim of scripture to finds in Peru and elsewhere. Rogan tests the claims and asks what hard proof would look like. Big bones and big claims make for a talk built for the curious.
